flashcards.front: What is the slope of the secant line?
flashcards.back: The ratio of the change in function value (delta f) to the change in x (delta x).
flashcards.explanation: The secant line connects two points; its slope is the rise over run, represented by delta f / delta x.

flashcards.front: How is the derivative defined using a limit?
flashcards.back: The limit of the secant slope as delta x approaches zero.
flashcards.explanation: The derivative is the instantaneous slope, found by shrinking the secant interval to zero.

flashcards.front: What is the formula for f'(x0)?
flashcards.back: limit as delta x approaches 0 of [f(x0 + delta x) - f(x0)] / delta x.
flashcards.explanation: This is the definition of the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient.

flashcards.front: What are the coordinates of point Q?
flashcards.explanation: Q is the point on the curve shifted by delta x from the original point P.
